title: Agreement count as complement of Hamming distance
statement:
Let $x, y : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{Bool}$ be two $n$-bit strings, with agreement count $\mathrm{agr}(x,y)$ the number of coordinates on which they coincide and $d_H(x,y)$ their Hamming distance (the number of coordinates on which they differ). Then, as an identity of integers,
\[
  \mathrm{agr}(x,y) = n - d_H(x,y).
\]
hypotheses_covered: x and y are n-bit strings (functions Fin n → Bool)
equality of integers after casting the natural-number agreement count to ℤ
replaced:
For any two $n$-bit strings $x$ and $y$, the agreement count satisfies
\[
  \mathrm{agreementCount}(x, y) = n - \mathrm{hammingDist}(x, y)
\]
as an equality of integers (after casting the natural numbers to $\mathbb{Z}$).
